paragraphs.text: This is a very strange board, and the 5-wheat sits off in no man's land.
I initially like 9-5-10: it gives wood and brick, and I see an interesting 8-10-to-8-5 continuation that I expect somebody to pursue. Alternatively, 8-10-4 adds sheep.

paragraphs.text: Comparing the lines, I do not see enough payoff in taking ore at 8-4-3. I prefer the 8-4-10 idea for access to a brick port, a 3:1, and sheep, perhaps pairing it with 6-5-11 and simply playing production.

I can imagine a favorable 5-10-to-8-10 follow-up, and I like the idea. I view the spoken 8-5-10 as having the same pips as 9-5-10, but sheep plus the prospect of picking up wood makes it sweeter, even though the spot still is not great.

paragraphs.text: For my own position, I still like the port plan, with the 3:1 and brick port as the appeal.
The 6-9-3 idea strikes me as smart because it offers many angles, including a route toward wood.

I am surprised fourth position has access to the best ore, but I cannot see an obvious way to exploit it. I consider 6-4-3, then focus on how poor the wheat is and how tough the position looks.

I hope Black eventually pairs brick with the best wood, perhaps through a six-heavy route or 6-4-11. I expect fourth position may take 8-4-3 as its better option, but I am unsure what follows; I briefly consider side-by-side placements, then reject that because it needs wood and a good port.

paragraphs.text: Overall it looks ugly: the sheep port seems bad and the ore port only okay. Another line is 8-4-3 with 6-4-11, taking much of the left side, trading toward a 3:1, and perhaps getting sheep plus value on ore trades; even then the ore-port upside feels limited and the choice is tough.
Then I notice 8-10-3, which I think opens two spots, including 8-4. I react that this is vicious and wild and think 8-4 might be available to us.
